issues.issue: The Interruption Of Computer Operations text is interleaved line by line with the Extended "Rental Value" provision, so the grant of coverage and its Causes of Loss conditions cannot be read as one provision.

The carry-forward sentence is corrupted ("If loss payment relaling to the first interruptlon does not enraey this amount, then the balance is ilé able ..."), obscuring how an unexhausted balance moves between policy years.

"[T]he applicable Limit of Insurance shown in the Declarations" for "any one occurrence" does not explain how the single blanket Business Income limit is applied when the occurrence affects several described premises.
It has to be applied to the Blanket Business Income entry in the Declarations (c004), which shows one $1,099,200 figure with no per-premises allocation.

The Kansas Changes endorsement (c259) replaces "The Appraisal Loss Condition" with a voluntary-only appraisal, and it is not clear whether that replacement reaches this separate Appraisal condition in the Business Income form, which allows appraisal on one party's demand.
"[Y]ou must resume all or part of your 'operations' as quickly as possible" sets an unmeasured duty whose breach is not defined anywhere in the form.

It overlaps with the Loss Determination rule for failure to resume (c226), which imposes a payment consequence for the same conduct without saying whether the duty here is also a condition of coverage.

The measure rests on "[t]he likely Net Income of the business if no physical loss or damage had occurred" and on operating expenses "necessary to resume 'operations' with the same quality of service", neither of which is defined or given a method of proof.

For a rental-value claim these Net Income inputs have to be matched against the "Rental Value" definition (c242), which measures loss by rental income from tenant occupancy rather than by business Net Income.

The reduction applies "to the extent you can resume your 'operations', in whole or in part, by using damaged or undamaged property ... at the described premises or elsewhere", without saying what makes such resumption possible or reasonable.
Recovery is capped by "the length of time it would have taken to resume 'operations' as quickly as possible", a hypothetical period the clause supplies no method of measuring.

This hypothetical-resumption cap sits alongside the "period of restoration" definition (c240), which fixes the end of coverage by when property "should be repaired ... with reasonable speed"; the two set different clocks for the same loss.

The penalty runs off Net Income and operating expenses "that would have been earned or incurred (had no loss occurred) ... for the 12 months following the inception", a hypothetical figure the clause gives no method of fixing.
It must be applied to the blanket Business Income limit in the Declarations (c004) at 100% coinsurance without any per-premises allocation of the underlying rental income.
The deduction list is interleaved with the worked example ("Step 1: . $400,000 x 50% = $200,000") and its numbering runs 1, 2, 3 then jumps, so several deductible expense categories are unreadable.
The Optional Coverages apply only "[i]f shown as applicable in the Declarations", and the Declarations for this policy (c004) show no Maximum Period Of Indemnity.
This 120-day cap would displace the "period of restoration" measure, but no Maximum Period Of Indemnity option is shown in the Declarations (c004).
No Monthly Limit Of Indemnity is shown in the Declarations (c004), so this Coinsurance carve-out has no field of operation.
The limit depends on "[t]he fraction shown in the Declarations for this Optional Coverage", and no such fraction appears in this policy's Declarations (c004).
Activation requires an Agreed Value shown in the Declarations, and none is shown for Business Income in this policy (c004).

The clause replaces the number "30" in the Extended Business Income provisions with "the number shown in the Declarations for this Optional Coverage", but no such number appears in this policy's Declarations.
"Operations" includes "the tenantability of the described premises", a term the form never defines even though it decides when a rental-value suspension begins and ends.

Limb b. applies only "if coverage for Business Income including 'Rental Value' or 'Rental Value' applies", and the Declarations entry (c004) does not identify which of the A.1 options (c189) was selected.

The period ends on "[t]he date when the property at the described premises should be repaired, rebuilt or replaced with reasonable speed and similar quality" — a hypothetical date fixed by "should" and "reasonable speed", neither of which the policy defines or benchmarks.
Paragraph a. as printed (72 hours for Business Income) is contradicted by the CP 15 56 Business Income Changes endorsement (c185), which makes the period begin immediately after the loss.

"Rental Value" is defined as Net Income "that would have been earned ... as rental income from tenant occupancy of the premises described in the Declarations as furnished and equipped by you", which does not say whether it is measured by pre-loss rents, market rents, or actual re-let experience.
It must be worked through the Loss Determination condition (c223), which measures loss by the business's Net Income and operating expenses rather than by rents.
"Suspension" turns on the premises being "rendered untenantable", a term the form leaves undefined although it triggers rental-value coverage.

"[A]ppears to be part of an effort to coerce a civilian population" makes the definition turn on appearances without saying to whom, and the $5 million carve-back cross-refers to a paragraph of another definition.
It replaces the Common Policy Condition on cancellation (c008) with substantially the same notice periods plus a duty to state reasons, leaving two versions of the same condition in the policy.
It requires 60 days' notice of nonrenewal, while the CGL condition When We Do Not Renew (c307) requires only 30 days' notice for that Coverage Part.
